name: Winter Hora Queen
body:
WINTER HORA QUEEN
CR 13

This beautiful woman appears enveloped in a cold, crystalline aura; her skin and hair are pale, her eyes and clothes as blue as deep ice.

XP 25,600
CG Medium fey
Init +9; Senses low-light vision; Perception +28
Aura paralyzing beauty (30 ft., DC 27)

DEFENSE

AC 28, touch 16, flat-footed 22 (+5 Dex, +1 dodge, +12 natural)
hp 187(22d6+110)
Fort +14, Ref +18, Will +16
DR 10/cold iron; Resist cold 20
Weaknesses winter bound

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 rime blades +17 (3d6+5 piercing +3d6 cold)
Ranged 2 rays of frost +17 (6d8 cold)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +16)

Constant—speak with animals, speak with plants
At will—know direction, light, pass without trace
1/day—alarm, bestow curse (DC 20), commune with nature, faerie fire, polar ray (DC 24), snowball (DC 17), true seeing

Druid Spells Prepared (CL 13th; concentration +16)

7th-level—control weather
6th-level—mass bear’s endurance, speak with waves
5th-level—cure critical wounds, stoneskin, wall of light (DC 19)
4th-level—creeping ice (DC 18), freedom of movement, ice storm, summon nature’s ally IV
3rd-level—cure moderate wounds, ice spears (DC 16), neutralize poison, protection from energy, quench (DC 16)
2nd-level—chill metal (DC 15), frigid touch, frost fall (DC 16), resist energy, summon nature’s ally II
1st-level—cure light wounds, endure elements, frostbite, longstrider, ice armor
0th-level—detect magic, guidance, resistance, stabilize

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 21, Con 20, Int 17, Wis 17, Cha 22
Base Atk +11; CMB +16, CMD 29
Feats Agile Maneuvers, Combat Casting, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Mobility, Sidestep, Spell Focus (evocation), Weapon Finesse, Weapon Focus (rime blade, ray of frost)
Skills Acrobatics +30, Climb +27, Diplomacy +31, Escape Artist +30, Knowledge (nature) +28, Perception +28, Sense Motive +28, Stealth +30, Survival +25
Languages Common, Elven, Sylvan; speak with animals, speak with plants
SQ winter’s wellness

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Paralyzing Beauty (Su)

This ability affects all humanoids within 30 feet of the winter hora queen. Those who look directly at the queen must succeed on a DC 27 Fortitude save or be exhausted for 1 minute and fatigued for 1 hour. The queen can suppress or resume this ability as a free action. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Spellcasting

The winter hora queen casts spells as a 13th-level druid, but can’t swap out prepared spells to cast summon spells.

Winter Bound (Su)

During summer months, the winter hora queen gains the sickened condition.

Winter’s Wellness (Su)

As an immediate action after a winter hora queen or an ally within 30 feet of the queen that it can see fails a saving throw, attack roll, or skill check, the queen grants an enhancement bonus to the saving throw based on the time of year. The bonus is +4 during the month of the winter solstice, +2 during the month before or after the winter solstice equinox, and +1 during any time other than the summer solstice month, during which this ability doesn’t function. The winter hora queen can’t use this ability again for 1d4 rounds.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate forests and mountains
Organization solitary or ring (1 + 1-24 winter horai)
Treasure double (2 rime blades, rimepelt, other treasure)

The Horai in the Greek myth were nymphs who danced around the Sun’s chariot, representing the seasons of the year and the hours of the day (the word “hour” derives from the Ancient Greek and Latin Hora). There were most commonly three of them: Thallo, Auxo, and Carpo (“Bloom” for Spring, “Increaser” for Summer, and “Reaper of Fruits” for Autumn). In other versions, they were the embodiment of the good effects of law and order (symbolized by Apollo) on the world of mortals, and their names were Eunomia (“Good Governance”), Dike (“Justice”), and Eirene (“Peace”). In Pathfinder’s rules, the stats for the Summer Hora and the Summer Hora Queen were given in the Faerie Bestiary: here we present horai for the remaining three seasons, and their respective Queens. Maybe the nymphs of Order could be discussed in a future issue of this magazine?

While most nymphs bond with a natural feature, such as a tree, pool, or cave, horai are rare nymphs associated with a specific time —a solstice or equinox— rather than a location. Horai erect simple astronomical calendars near their home, which they use to mark the moment when the sun reaches its highest, median, and lowest point in the sky.

An hora tied to the summer solstice grows more powerful as the sun reaches its height, while an hora tied to the winter solstice is sickly and weak. The opposite holds true for winter horai, who are weak in summer and strong in winter. Meanwhile, autumn and spring horai draw power near the autumnal and vernal equinoxes, becoming weaker around the opposite equinox.
